claims.assertion: The driver never reached the pickup point: his closest approach was 319 m at 08:46:50 and the GPS record states he never came within 200 m of the pickup point.

The driver pressed "I'm Here" at 08:47:20 while GPS put him 351 m from the pickup point, and he stayed within 200 m for 0 s after the tap, so NS-1 (ii) fails and the platform never recorded him at the pickup point at all.

While he waited he remained stationary 350 m from the pickup point (08:47:00–08:51:00), never closing the remaining distance to the pickup point, so the whole wait was spent outside the pickup radius.

The rider was in fact at the pickup point and said so at 08:48 ("I'm at the pickup point, no car here. Where are you?"), directly contradicting the driver's 08:47 claim that he had "reached already"; the rider never showed up because the car was not there.

The driver's written statement that he "waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup" is a claim contradicted by the GPS and timeline records of his position (319–351 m away, 0 s inside 200 m), so the system records govern and his statement cannot establish NS-1.
Because NS-1 (i)/(ii)/(iii) are not satisfied — in particular he was not at the pickup location when he tapped — the $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full to the rider.
The driver's tap of "I'm Here" while GPS placed him 351 m from the pickup point is an abuse of the arrival/waiting button, which warrants a flag_account referral alongside the refund.

The chat record is complete and every message is timestamped, so the sequence (driver's arrival claim 08:47 → rider's denial 08:48 → driver's cancellation notice 08:50) can be determined without resorting to reconstruction, and no safety escalation is triggered by any message.

weaknesses: The driver did wait 4 minutes (F2) and cancelled 7 minutes after acceptance (F3), so the other side will argue he made a genuine effort and that the rider simply did not come to him; the 350 m offset could be argued as a nearby but mis-pinned location.

The rider's own message (F9) is the only record that the rider was at the pickup point; there is no rider-side GPS fact placing the rider within 200 m, so the driver can argue the rider's presence is unproven.

The driver has an unblemished profile — 3.7 years, 4.85 rating, 992 trips, 0 disputes upheld (F17) — and the rider's profile shows 1 dispute (F16), which the other side may use to suggest the complaint is opportunistic.

No traffic or weather factor (F13, F14, F15) helps the driver, but equally there is no independent record of how long the rider had been waiting before 08:47, so the waiting-fee/no-show timeline cannot be reconstructed from the rider's side.

claims.assertion: The driver never reached the pickup point: his closest approach was 319 m at 08:46:50 and the GPS record states he never came within 200 m of the pickup point.

The driver pressed "I'm Here" at 08:47:20 while GPS put him 351 m from the pickup point, and he stayed within 200 m for 0 s after the tap, so NS-1 (ii) fails and the platform never recorded him at the pickup point at all.

While he waited he remained stationary 350 m from the pickup point (08:47:00–08:51:00), never closing the remaining distance to the pickup point, so the whole wait was spent outside the pickup radius.

The rider was in fact at the pickup point and said so at 08:48 ("I'm at the pickup point, no car here. Where are you?"), directly contradicting the driver's 08:47 claim that he had "reached already"; the rider never showed up because the car was not there.

The driver's written statement that he "waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup" is a claim contradicted by the GPS and timeline records of his position (319–351 m away, 0 s inside 200 m), so the system records govern and his statement cannot establish NS-1.
Because NS-1 (i)/(ii)/(iii) are not satisfied — in particular he was not at the pickup location when he tapped — the $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full to the rider.
The driver's tap of "I'm Here" while GPS placed him 351 m from the pickup point is an abuse of the arrival/waiting button, which warrants a flag_account referral alongside the refund.

The chat record is complete and every message is timestamped, so the sequence (driver's arrival claim 08:47 → rider's denial 08:48 → driver's cancellation notice 08:50) can be determined without resorting to reconstruction, and no safety escalation is triggered by any message.

weaknesses: The driver did wait 4 minutes (F2) and cancelled 7 minutes after acceptance (F3), so the other side will argue he made a genuine effort and that the rider simply did not come to him; the 350 m offset could be argued as a nearby but mis-pinned location.

The rider's own message (F9) is the only record that the rider was at the pickup point; there is no rider-side GPS fact placing the rider within 200 m, so the driver can argue the rider's presence is unproven.

The driver has an unblemished profile — 3.7 years, 4.85 rating, 992 trips, 0 disputes upheld (F17) — and the rider's profile shows 1 dispute (F16), which the other side may use to suggest the complaint is opportunistic.

No traffic or weather factor (F13, F14, F15) helps the driver, but equally there is no independent record of how long the rider had been waiting before 08:47, so the waiting-fee/no-show timeline cannot be reconstructed from the rider's side.

claims.assertion: The driver did tap "I'm Here" at 08:47:20 and then remained stationary at a fixed point for the four minutes 08:47:00–08:51:00 before cancelling, so the driver did genuinely wait before cancelling rather than cancelling instantly.

The wait was real but short of the required span: the tap was at 08:47:20 and the cancellation at 08:51:00, only about 3 min 40 s, and the record shows the driver stayed within 200 m of the pickup for 0 s after the tap, so NS-1 (iii)'s continuous in-radius wait of more than 3 minutes is not established.

The driver was never at the pickup point: the closest approach was 319 m at 08:46:50, never within 200 m, and the stationary position was 350 m from the pickup, while the platform never recorded an arrival (driver_arrived_at is null); NS-1 (ii) therefore fails and the $6.61 no-show fee cannot stand.

The driver's own written statement that he waited at the pickup is a claim, not evidence, because it conflicts with the GPS records showing he was 319–351 m away; on the system-record-first rule the GPS record governs.
The driver pressed the arrival button while 351 m from the pickup point, which is outside the 200 m arrival radius, so the arrival-button abuse limb of NS-2 is engaged on the face of the record.
The rider messaged at 08:48 that she was at the pickup point with no car there, and the driver's stationary position 350 m away corroborates that she was at the correct place while the car was not.
Fair weather (0.0 mm rain), no traffic incidents and no speed-band records on the route during the trip window remove any external explanation for the driver's failure to reach the pickup point.

The driver has a long clean record (3.7 years, rating 4.85, 992 trips in 90 days, 0 disputes and 0 upheld), which is a mitigating fact to be weighed against any account flag, but under the policy profile facts cannot decide the case.
The only sum in dispute is the $6.61 cancellation fee on record (surge 1.0×, no other add-on), so the refund quantum is fixed by the fare record and is not in dispute as to amount.

weaknesses: The GPS record is against us at every point: F1 (closest approach 319 m, never within 200 m), F2 (stationary 350 m from pickup) and F5 (tap at 351 m, 0 s inside 200 m) make NS-1 (ii) and (iii) impossible to satisfy, and the rider will rely on exactly these facts.
F4 (driver_arrived_at is null) plus F5 (tap outside the radius) invite a flag_account under NS-2 for arrival-button abuse, so the driver is exposed to more than a refund of the fee.

The driver's clean profile (F17) is mitigation only and cannot defeat the mandatory refund that NS-2 produces once NS-1's conditions fail.

The flag is a matter for Ryde's account review on the record, but the rider's citation of NS-6 is inapposite: NS-6 governs the $5.00 waiting fee, not the arrival-button abuse limb of NS-2, and no waiting fee was charged here (F6 shows only the $6.61 cancellation fee, surge 1.0×, F7). Mitigation remains that the driver waited four minutes and cancelled seven minutes after acceptance with a 3.7-year, 0-upheld record (F2, F3, F17), and under NS-2 profile facts cannot decide the case.

The completeness point is common ground (F11); I note only that the rider's own timing claim in that chat (F9) is the sole record of her arrival, which the rider's weaknesses also concede, and that no message in F8–F10 reads as a threat or dangerous-driving allegation, so no SAFE-1/SAFE-2 escalation arises.

Withdrawn as a defence of the fee and retained only as mitigation: the tap and the four-minute wait are real (F5, F2) but they were spent 351–350 m from the pickup point, so under NS-1 (ii)-(iii) they cannot support the $6.61 charge.

Your message that you were waiting with no car in sight matched the location data, so the fee shouldn't have been charged. No further action is needed from you. Thanks for flagging this, and sorry for the trouble.
